Free replacement implemented instead: apps/web/app/lib/auth/pwned-password.ts checks the password against Have I Been Pwned by k-anonymity (only the first 5 hex chars of SHA-1 leave the server) and apps/web/app/lib/auth/password-policy.ts rejects a breached password when setting one. 13 unit tests, written RED first. VERIFIED against the live service on 2026-09-20: "password" -> found (2130 rows in range), a random 32-char string -> not found, and 152 of those rows were zero-count padding, so the count>0 check is load-bearing. Fails open: service down, non-200 or timeout means the password is accepted, so an outage never locks anyone out. Covers only password CREATION in /auth (setPassword, finishRecovery); it does not re-check existing passwords and is not equivalent to the platform feature.

openFindings: P2 -> FIXED in migration 0053 (Codex review of PR #15 raised it as P1): threads_select_own_supplier no longer lets a supplier owner read a thread without the plan-membership predicate; it now requires supplier_can_access_order (current plan contains the company). REPRODUCED first: 3 new tests in privileged-rpc-authorization.test.ts failed (a supplier dropped from the plan, including its owner, still read the thread and could insert a message), GREEN after 0053, whole db suite 184/184 locally. Thread and message ROWS are still never deleted (history kept); only access is closed, and A -> B -> A restores it for A and closes it for B. Not applied to production: needs migration 0053 (along with 0051, 0052). Original finding: 0051 lets a buyer re-point the plan between proposed variants and ensure_order_supplier_threads_on_plan_change only adds threads.

P3 -> FIXED in migration 0054: a new trigger (audit_order_plan_repoint) writes an order_stage_events row when approved_plan_id changes while the state does not, naming both variants with their kind and total, and the buyer as actor. REPRODUCED first: 2 of 3 new tests failed (no row after select_order_plan, none after a direct re-point), GREEN after the migration; db suite 187/187 locally. from_state equals to_state because this is a decision inside a stage, not a transition, and to_state is NOT NULL. Deliberate gaps: a change made with no auth.uid() (service role, seed, migrations) is skipped rather than attributed to an invented actor, and a combined plan+state change is left to the existing transition trigger to avoid a duplicate row. EXECUTE was revoked explicitly, because 0043 grants it to authenticated for every NEW function; the all-trigger-functions test in function-privileges.test.ts covers it. Not applied to production.

P3 -> REPRODUCED, and CLOSED WITHOUT A CODE CHANGE. packages/db/src/__tests__/plan-repoint-race.test.ts drives the interleaving deterministically (A re-points to planB while it is proposed and holds the transaction; B supersedes planB and commits; A commits). Outcome: the order DOES end up pointing at a superseded plan. A row lock would not change that, because staff can supersede immediately after a legitimate re-point - the window is inherent to check-then-act, not to the missing lock, and a lock inside the order guard would add deadlock risk on a hot path. What matters is that the system stays consistent and the buyer is not stuck, and the test proves both: the pointer still references a plan of the same request, approving the superseded plan is refused with a stated rule, and the buyer can re-point to the other proposed variant and does. The RPC path was already safe (orders FOR UPDATE then plans FOR UPDATE).

P3 -> ACCEPTED as a known limit, recorded rather than changed. is_staff_user(uuid) lets any signed-in user ask whether an arbitrary UUID belongs to QAJET staff. RLS policies need it for other users ids, and SECURITY DEFINER is what lets it read users past RLS. Exploiting it requires already knowing a UUID, which is not enumerable, and the answer is a single boolean about role, not personal data. Narrowing it to callers who already share an order or thread would add a join to a function used inside policies on a hot path, for no reachable gain. Documented in docs/security/security-definer-inventory.md. Revisit if user ids ever become guessable or appear in URLs shared outside the company.

P1 -> FIXED (owner chose warn-and-mark over making the tick required, so a supplier may still answer "this is the price, but I cannot take it on"). The quote form now explains the consequence beside the unticked box on the first click and does not submit; the second submits. Ticking clears the warning immediately because it is derived. The same gate is on the signed-link form. Afterwards the supplier sees the pending state on the RFQ page and on their home page, with the honest part that only QAJET can reopen it. The concierge now sees such an order marked on the board and in the Exceptions queue with the item that blocks it. Rejection policy unchanged. Commits d0a529a and 51e5bbc; e2e specs supplier-journey (F1) and concierge-journey (F1, F6) cover it. Still open from the same audit: F2 and F3 remain fixme.

P1 (product decision, ASSUMPTION about the platform): if the Vercel function body limit of about 4.5 MB applies, attachments between ~4.5 and 10 MB fail in production even after the Server Action limit fix. Options: upload straight to Storage with a signed upload URL (removes the limit and the function from the path, larger change) or state an honest lower limit in the form (small change). Verify the actual limit on the deployed project before choosing.

defectsFixed.summary: The buyer button "choose another variant" (apps/web/app/buyer/orders/[id]/_plan-alternatives.tsx -> selectPlan -> select_order_plan) always failed. The guard refuses with RAISE EXCEPTION (SQLSTATE P0001), which actionFailure classifies as a business rejection, so the buyer saw the internal sentence "Покупатель не может менять внутренние поля заказа" with NO supportId. (An earlier version of this note said a generic error with a supportId; that was wrong, corrected 2026-09-20 after reading action-result.ts.) The message is confusing and, having no code, could not be found through the support-id runbook.
defectsFixed.cause: select_order_plan (0037) updates orders.approved_plan_id for the buyer, but guard_order_actor allowed a buyer to change only state and closing fields in every version from 0020 to 0041. Inside a SECURITY DEFINER function current_setting(role) is still authenticated, so the guard saw a direct buyer edit and raised "Покупатель не может менять внутренние поля заказа". Only the EXECUTE grant was ever tested, never a buyer actually calling it.
defectsFixed.evidence: REPRODUCED by privileged-rpc-authorization.test.ts against real PostgreSQL: RED (2 of 42 failed) before the migration, GREEN after. Five of six guard conditions are mutation-checked; the sixth (v_buyer inside v_repoint) is an equivalent mutant.
defectsFixed.fix: The invariant now lives in guard_order_actor: a buyer may change approved_plan_id only before approval, to a proposed plan of the same request, in the same stage, with no other column changed. A session-flag design (like qajet.stage_reason) was rejected because it would be a forgeable privilege.
